Vedanta lines up $25 bn investment over next three years for organic growth
items.summary:
The Vedanta Group has lined up USD 25 billion in investments over the next three years to expand capacities across its existing businesses through organic growth and brownfield expansions, a top company official said.
Vedanta founder and chairman Anil Agarwal, who was in the city on Wednesday, said the conglomerate would focus on its existing assets for growth, while remaining open to acquiring public sector assets if opportunities arise.
"Current capex plans are for organic growth in aluminium, copper, zinc, oil and gas. All will be brownfield expansions," he said.
"We are going to invest around USD 25 billion," Agarwal said.
The capital expenditure would also support Vedanta's ambition to become one of the world's largest mining companies in critical metals, and emerge as a leading silver producer within three to four years, he said.
The group, which comprises 10 major companies, aims to grow its overall business from USD 30 billion to USD 50 billion within three years, Agarwal

City Union Bank Q2 FY27 results: Net profit rises 26% to ₹416 crore
items.summary:
City Union Bank on Wednesday reported a 26 per cent rise in net profit at Rs 416 crore for the second quarter ended September 2026.
The bank had a net profit of Rs 329 crore in the July-September quarter of last fiscal.
Interest income grew 27 per cent to Rs 2,092 crore in the second quarter of FY27, up from Rs 1,653 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26.
Net non-performing assets improved to 0.48 per cent in the September quarter of FY27, from 0.90 per cent in the year-ago period.
Shares of City Union Bank were trading at Rs 215.55, up 1.05 per cent over the previous close, on the BSE.

items.summary:
Leading cinema exhibitor PVR INOX on Wednesday reported a two-fold increase in its consolidated net profit to Rs 263.1 crore for the September quarter, led by strong box office performance.
The company reported a net profit of Rs 105.5 crore for the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
PVR INOX revenue from operations rose 16.97 per cent to Rs 2,105.1 crore in the September quarter of FY27, the company said, its "highest-ever quarterly revenue". It posted revenue of Rs 1,799.6 crore in the corresponding period in the last fiscal.
Total expenses were Rs 1,788.2 crore in the September quarter, up 5.86 per cent.
The company recorded its highest-ever quarterly box office performance, with admissions rising 4 per cent to 4.63 crore. Its occupancy improved to 30.4 per cent from 28.7 per cent in the year-ago period. PVR Inox said this is also its "its highest-ever quarterly" figure.

PVR INOX Q2 profit up 2-fold at ₹263.1 cr on strong box office performance
items.summary:
Leading cinema exhibitor PVR INOX on Wednesday reported a two-fold increase in its consolidated net profit to Rs 263.1 crore for the September quarter, led by strong box office performance.
The company reported a net profit of Rs 105.5 crore for the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
PVR INOX revenue from operations rose 16.97 per cent to Rs 2,105.1 crore in the September quarter of FY27, the company said, its "highest-ever quarterly revenue". It posted revenue of Rs 1,799.6 crore in the corresponding period in the last fiscal.
Total expenses were Rs 1,788.2 crore in the September quarter, up 5.86 per cent.
The company recorded its highest-ever quarterly box office performance, with admissions rising 4 per cent to 4.63 crore. Its occupancy improved to 30.4 per cent from 28.7 per cent in the year-ago period. PVR Inox said this is also its "its highest-ever quarterly" figure.

items.summary:
Bajaj Auto on Tuesday reported a 35 per cent jump in standalone profit after tax to Rs 3,354 crore in the three months to September compared to the corresponding quarter of the last financial year.
The company had posted a standalone profit after tax of Rs 2,480 crore in the July-September period of FY 26.
Revenue from operations for the quarter under review stood at Rs 20,003 crore, up 34 per cent year-on-year from Rs 14,922 crore in the September quarter last year.
EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) climbed 37 per cent to Rs 4,172 crore in Q2 FY27 against Rs 3,052 crore in the same quarter of FY26, the company said in a statement. EBITDA Margin rose 40 basis points to 20.9 per cent in Q2 FY27 against 20.5 per cent in the second quarter of the year earlier, the company said.
